people.Pulastya: A mind-born son of Brahma (a Prajapati); grandfather of Ravana through his son Vishrava.
people.Vishrava: Sage son of Pulastya; father of Kubera by Ilavida and of Ravana and his siblings by the rakshasi Kaikasi.

Kaikasi.note: Rakshasi wife of Vishrava, daughter of the demon Sumali; mother of Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and Vibhishana.

people.Kubera: Son of Vishrava and Ilavida; the yaksha lord of wealth who first ruled Lanka, until his half-brother Ravana drove him out.

Ravana.note: The ten-headed rakshasa king of Lanka; a mighty devotee of Shiva and master of the Vedas whose abduction of Sita brought his doom. By name — penance for boons from Brahma (near-invincibility, but not against men or vanaras, which he thought beneath asking), seizing Lanka from his half-brother Kubera and the Pushpaka chariot with it, composing the Shiva Tandava Stotram after Shiva pinned him under Kailasa for trying to lift it, Surpanakha's mutilation drawing him to Panchavati, the golden-deer ruse and Sita's abduction, Jatayu's failed rescue, Vibhishana's defection when he refused to return her, the burning of Lanka by Hanuman, Kumbhakarna and Indrajit dying in the war before him, and his own death to Rama's Brahmastra.

people.Kumbhakarna: Giant brother of Ravana, cursed to sleep six months at a time; woken for the war, he was slain by Rama.

Shurpanakha.note: Sister of Ravana whose courting of Rama and Lakshmana, and the loss of her nose, set the war in motion.

people.Vibhishana: Youngest brother of Ravana; righteous, he deserted to Rama and was crowned king of Lanka after the war.
people.Indrajit: Meghanada, son of Ravana and Mandodari; he once defeated Indra himself, hence his name, and was slain by Lakshmana.
people.Atikaya: Son of Ravana and Mandodari; a colossal warrior slain by Lakshmana.
people.Akshayakumara: Young son of Ravana, slain by Hanuman in the burning of Lanka.
people.Kumbha: Son of Kumbhakarna, killed in the war.
people.Nikumbha: Son of Kumbhakarna, killed in the war.
people.Sumali: A rakshasa lord of the elder line of Lanka; father of Kaikasi, whom he gave to the sage Vishrava to sire sons who might rival the devas.

Narantaka.note: Son of Ravana, a fierce warrior slain by the vanara Angada.

Devantaka.note: Son of Ravana, slain by Hanuman.

Trishira.note: Three-headed son of Ravana, slain by Hanuman.

Sukesha.note: An elder rakshasa lord; father of Sumali and Malyavan.

Malyavan.note: Grand old rakshasa, brother of Sumali; the wise elder who counselled Ravana to return Sita and make peace.

Prahasta.note: Son of Sumali and maternal uncle of Ravana; chief commander of Lanka's army, slain by the vanara Nila.

Trijata.note: Daughter of Vibhishana and Sarama; the kind rakshasi who watched over Sita and foretold Rama's victory.

Ahiravana.note: Rakshasa king of Patala, a sorcerer who carried Rama and Lakshmana off in their sleep to sacrifice them to his goddess. He raised the fish-born Makardhwaja and made him his gatekeeper, and Hanuman killed him. The retellings differ over whether he is Ravana's son or his brother, and often pair him with Mahiravana. Krittivasi Ramayana; Ananda Ramayana

Mali.note: Third son of Sukesha, with Malyavan and Sumali; one of the three rakshasa brothers who held Lanka before Ravana. Killed by Vishnu in the war that drove his brothers south and left the city empty for Kubera. Ram 7.5-7.8

Nalakubara.note: Son of Kubera and husband of Rambha. When Ravana forced her he cursed him: if he ever took another woman against her will his head would burst into seven pieces -- which is precisely why Ravana could hold Sita a year in the ashoka grove and never touch her. Rām 7.26

Manigriva.note: Son of Kubera, brother of Nalakubara. Narada came on the two of them drunk and naked in the Ganga with the apsaras, who covered themselves and were forgiven while the brothers did not think to, and cursed them into a pair of arjuna trees until Krishna should free them. They stood a hundred years in Nanda's yard, until the infant, roped to a mortar for stealing butter, crawled between the trunks and pulled them both down. SB 10.9-10

Vidyutjihva.note: A Kalakeya danava, husband of Shurpanakha. Ravana killed him in the war on the Kalakeyas without knowing whose husband he was, and gave his sister the freedom of Lanka and of Dandaka afterwards by way of amends. Uttara Kanda 24

Shambhukumara.note: Son of Shurpanakha and Vidyutjihva. He was standing on his head at his austerities in the Dandaka thicket when Lakshmana, clearing ground, cut through it and took his head off without ever seeing him — which, in the tellings that give her a reason, is why his mother came to Panchavati. Uttara Kanda; Adhyatma Ramayana

Raka.note: Daughter of Sumali and another of Vishrava's wives; mother of Khara, Dushana and Kumbhinasi. The Uttara Kanda's account of Vishrava's household is not tidy and the reference works differ on her; what is constant everywhere is that Khara is Ravana's half-brother and Shurpanakha's protector. Uttara Kanda 24

Khara.note: Half-brother of Ravana, set over the fourteen thousand rakshasas of Janasthana in Dandaka with Dushana under him and Shurpanakha in his keeping. She came to him with her nose and ears cut off; he sent fourteen, then all fourteen thousand, and Rama killed every one of them alone in an afternoon while Lakshmana held Sita in a cave. It is the news of that afternoon, brought to Lanka, that turns Ravana toward Sita at all. Rama 3.19-30

Dushana.note: Khara's brother and second at Janasthana; killed with him and with the whole fourteen thousand in the same engagement. Rama 3.19-30

Kumbhinasi.note: Daughter of Vishrava and Raka, sister of Khara. The asura Madhu carried her off; Ravana came to kill him for it and let him live at her asking — which is the whole reason Madhu's son Lavana was still alive an age later for Shatrughna to kill, and so the reason Mathura came into the hands of Rama's brothers. Uttara Kanda 61

MadhuAsura.name: Madhu
MadhuAsura.note: An asura who carried off Kumbhinasi, Ravana's half-sister, and was spared at her own asking when Ravana came for him. He held Madhuvana on the Yamuna, and the trident he had been given passed from him to his son. Uttara Kanda 61

Lavanasura.name: Lavana
Lavanasura.note: Son of Madhu and Kumbhinasi, who held Madhuvana with his father's trident and ate the people of the country around it until the rishis of the Yamuna went to Ayodhya about him. Shatrughna took Rama's own bow, waited until the trident was set down, and killed him — then built his city on the ground, which is Mathura, where Krishna is born an age later. It is the one thing the fourth brother does alone. Uttara Kanda 61-70

unions.note: Nalakubara was carried here as Kubera's brother for want of anywhere else to hang him; SB 10.9 makes him Kubera's son, and he now sits under his father with Manigriva.
Ahiravana's people found the child in the fish and brought him up. Krittivasi Ramayana
He took her on her way to her husband, and Nalakubara's curse for it is what saved Sita. Rām 7.26
Uttara Kanda 24. Cited rather than read; see Raka's note.
Uttara Kanda 61. He carried her off and she then asked her brother to spare him; the taking is what the record is, and what she did afterwards does not unmake it.
